title: Quasi-coherent modules and ideals along a closed immersion of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Here closed immersion means representable by closed immersions of schemes after every base change to a scheme [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Work on the small etale sites, with module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and the direct image $i_*$ along the induced morphism of topoi [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Then $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is quasi-coherent over $\mathcal O_X$, the map $i^\sharp:\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective, and its kernel $\mathcal I$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_X$. The functor $i_*:\operatorname{QCoh}(Z)\to\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$, with scalar action through $i^\sharp$, is exact and fully faithful, with essential image precisely the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules $\mathcal F$ such that $\mathcal I\mathcal F=0$. The last condition means that multiplication by every local section of $\mathcal I$ on every local section of $\mathcal F$ is zero. No nilpotence, finite-type, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First verify the hypotheses of the general quasi-coherent pushforward theorem. On each affine scheme test $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, representable closedness gives $Z\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ for an ideal $J$, so this source is quasi-compact. These quotient maps are monomorphisms: two ring maps out of $R/J$ agreeing after $R\to R/J$ agree on every residue class. Checking this on scheme charts shows that $i$ is a monomorphism of sheaves, hence its diagonal is an isomorphism and is a closed immersion on every scheme test. Thus $i$ is quasi-compact and separated in the terminology of the cited locality node. The general pushforward theorem now makes $i_*G$ quasi-coherent for every quasi-coherent $G$. In particular apply it to $G=\mathcal O_Z$, whose one-generator presentation makes it quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tags 04CG (lemma-closed-immersion-quasi-compact), 04CH (lemma-closed-immersion-separated), and 03M9 (lemma-pushforward); the quotient-ring verification is written out.

proof.text: For every affine etale scheme chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$, the base-changed closed immersion has source $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$. The etale direct-image restriction comparison identifies $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)(U)$ with $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)=R/J$, and $i^\sharp(U)$ with $R\twoheadrightarrow R/J$. Every etale test scheme is covered by affine opens, so each local section of $i_*\mathcal O_Z$ has local lifts to $\mathcal O_X$. This proves surjectivity as a map of sheaves, without asserting surjectivity on arbitrary nonaffine section rings. Its kernel $\mathcal I$ is an ideal by multiplicativity. Both source and target are quasi-coherent (step 1), so the cited kernel theorem makes $\mathcal I$ quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals), first paragraph of proof; Tag 03LX for etale restriction; Tag 03M1 for kernels.

proof.text: Apply the exactness and conservativity clause of [lem-sfb-space-stalk-ideal-pullback] using identity thickenings of the space in question and the identity square; their ideals are zero and hence square-zero, so this clause applies to every algebraic space without imposing a square-zero hypothesis on the present immersion. At a geometric point $\bar z$ of $Z$ write $\bar x=i\bar z$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, and $B=\mathcal O_{Z,\bar z}$. The closed direct-image stalk comparison, applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal O_Z$, identifies $(i_*\mathcal O_Z)_{\bar x}$ with $B$. Since this comparison is restriction of germs it respects products and identifies the structure map with $A\to B$. Exactness of module stalks applied to step 2 gives $B=A/\mathcal I_{\bar x}$. At a geometric point outside $Z$, the direct-image stalk is zero, and the same exact sequence gives $\mathcal I_{\bar x}=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$.

source.place: Tag 0DK1 (lemma-stalk-push-closed), corrected subscripts, and Tag 03MB; spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K5 and sites-modules.tex Tag 04EQ.

proof.text: Use the canonical adjunction $i^*\dashv i_*$ of module sheaves. The ordinary-complex clause of the cited stalk-tensor calculus gives $(i^*H)_{\bar z}=H_{\bar x}\otimes_A B$: specialize its square to $f=\mathrm{id}_X$, $g=i$, so $g'=i$, and put $H$ in degree zero. For $H=i_*G$, the closed stalk comparison makes the counit at $\bar z$ the map $G_{\bar z}\otimes_A B\to G_{\bar z}$, $m\otimes b\mapsto bm$. As $A\twoheadrightarrow B$ by step 3, its inverse is $m\mapsto m\otimes1$: lifting $b$ to $a\in A$ gives $bm\otimes1=m\otimes b$. The stalk criterion proves the counit is an isomorphism for every $G$. It follows that $i_*$ is fully faithful: the inverse to the map on Hom sets sends $\alpha:i_*G\to i_*G'$ to $\varepsilon_{G'}\circ i^*(\alpha)\circ\varepsilon_G^{-1}$; naturality and the adjunction triangle identities give both inverse equations. Restricting to the full quasi-coherent subcategories gives the required full faithfulness.

source.place: Tag 04CJ (lemma-i-star-equivalence), proof of (2) and full faithfulness in (3); sites-modules.tex Tag 05V5. Tensor inverse and Hom inverse are explicit.

proof.text: Every $i_*G$ is annihilated by $\mathcal I$: a local element of the kernel of $\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ acts by zero under the specified scalar action. Conversely let $F$ be quasi-coherent and $\mathcal IF=0$. The cited pullback theorem makes $G=i^*F$ quasi-coherent. Consider the canonical unit $\eta_F:F\to i_*i^*F$. At $\bar x=i\bar z$, the closed stalk comparison and the ordinary pullback-stalk formula used in step 4 identify its stalk with $F_{\bar x}\to F_{\bar x}\otimes_A(A/\mathcal I_{\bar x})$, $m\mapsto m\otimes1$; this normalization follows from the local-tensor description of the canonical adjunction. Since $\mathcal I_{\bar x}F_{\bar x}=0$, the inverse sends $m\otimes\bar a$ to $am$, independent of the lift of $\bar a$. Outside $Z$, step 3 and $\mathcal IF=0$ give $F_{\bar x}=0$, while the closed direct-image stalk is zero. Thus all stalk maps of $\eta_F$ are isomorphisms, so $F\cong i_*G$. This proves the essential-image assertion.

source.place: Tag 04CJ (lemma-i-star-equivalence), essential-image argument; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03GA and sites-modules.tex Tag 05V5.

proof.text: Finally take a short exact sequence of quasi-coherent modules on $Z$. At a geometric point of $X$ on $Z$, its direct-image stalk sequence is the original exact stalk sequence by the natural closed stalk comparisons. At a point outside $Z$ it is the zero sequence. To reflect exactness, take each kernel modulo image in the direct-image sequence. Exact stalk functors send this obstruction module to zero, and joint detection of isomorphisms applied to its map to zero forces the obstruction module itself to be zero. Thus the direct-image sequence is exact in all $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Kernels and cokernels of maps between quasi-coherent modules are the same as in all module sheaves by the cited closure theorem, so the sequence is exact in $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ as well. This proves exactness, with no finiteness or nilpotence assumptions.

source.place: Tag 04CJ (lemma-i-star-equivalence), part (3); exactness supplied explicitly from Tag 0DK1 and spaces-properties.tex Tag 04K5.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03MB and 04CJ, with the geometric-stalk proof of unit, counit and exactness expanded using 0DK1, 04K5, 04EQ and 05V5.

lean.statement: theorem closedImmersion_quasiCoherent_modules {S : Scheme.{u}} {Z X : AlgebraicSpace S} (i : Z ⟶ X) (hi : IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsClosedImmersion p.left) i.hom.hom) : ∃ (hqc : ∀ M : Z.Modules, M.IsQuasicoherent → ((moduleDirectImage i).obj M).IsQuasicoherent) (I : QuasiCoherentIdeal X), ((moduleDirectImage i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.structureSheaf)).IsQuasicoherent ∧ Epi (moduleStructureMap i) ∧ I.val = kernelSubobject (moduleStructureMap i) ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits (quasiCoherentDirectImage i hqc) ∧ PreservesFiniteColimits (quasiCoherentDirectImage i hqc) ∧ (quasiCoherentDirectImage i hqc).Full ∧ (quasiCoherentDirectImage i hqc).Faithful ∧ (∀ F : QCoh X, (∃ G : QCoh Z, Nonempty (F ≅ (quasiCoherentDirectImage i hqc).obj G)) ↔ ∀ (V : X.EtaleSite) (a : (I.val : X.Modules).val.obj (op V)) (m : F.obj.val.obj (op V)), (I.val.arrow.val.app (op V) a) • m = 0)
lean.note: The helper is the actual ObjectProperty.lift of moduleDirectImage through the existing full QCoh subcategories. The theorem supplies its quasi-coherence proof, then states exactness as preservation of finite limits and finite colimits, full faithfulness, and the essential image by local ideal annihilation. The ideal is the existing QuasiCoherentIdeal with underlying subobject equal to kernelSubobject of the existing canonical moduleStructureMap; Epi means sheaf surjectivity, not sectionwise surjectivity. Only lean and additions of the two already-landed definition dependencies change.
